description: SevvaAI is a solo project for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the “Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map” challenge. The name comes from “Sevvai” (செவ்வாய்), the Tamil name for Mars, combined with AI (Artificial Intelligence). SevvaAI aims to make Martian exploration more accessible through AI-assisted maps, mission data, scientific information, and intelligent exploration planning.
summary:
SEVVAAI is an interactive Mars Exploration Command System that makes NASA planetary science accessible through a web-based mission experience. Users can explore Mars missions, command a 3D Perseverance rover across terrain derived from planetary elevation datasets, investigate scientific targets using simulated NASA instrument workflows, and interact with SARA, an intelligent mission companion.

The platform combines NASA and JPL mission information, USGS planetary terrain data, interactive 3D visualization, rover navigation, science activities, and mission telemetry in one application. SARA provides contextual guidance and scientific explanations, including offline assistance.

SEVVAAI aims to make planetary exploration more engaging and understandable for students, educators, and space enthusiasts, especially those using ordinary laptops rather than high-end gaming computers.
details:
What SEVVAAI Does

SEVVAAI is a web-based Mars exploration platform built around an interactive mission-control experience.

The application currently supports five spacecraft profiles: Perseverance, Curiosity, InSight, Phoenix, and Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO). Its primary interactive 3D experience focuses on the Perseverance rover at Jezero Crater.

Users can:

  • Explore mission information, spacecraft specifications, and landing-site details.
  • Drive a 3D Perseverance rover using keyboard controls across a Martian terrain environment.
  • Navigate toward scientific targets and interact with simulated instrument investigations.
  • Learn about Mastcam-Z, SuperCam, RIMFAX, MOXIE, and the rover's coring system.
  • Monitor rover position, heading, terrain slope, distance travelled, and mission progress.
  • Record discoveries in a digital Field Journal and Sample Vault.
  • Explore planetary maps and mission locations.
  • Ask SARA (Smart Autonomous Research Assistant) for scientific explanations, navigation assistance, and mission guidance.

How It Works

The application uses Python and Streamlit for its interface and mission workflows. Three.js provides the interactive WebGL rover simulation. The rover's movement, terrain interaction, telemetry, and mission progress are coordinated between the browser and the application.

SARA provides contextual mission assistance through an offline guidance engine, with optional cloud AI integration when an appropriate API key is configured.

Data and Scientific Foundation

The project incorporates NASA and JPL mission information and planetary datasets, including Mars terrain and elevation resources. USGS HiRISE and Context Camera (CTX) terrain products support the Martian surface visualization.

The application distinguishes scientific information and source-derived terrain from simplified gameplay mechanics. Real rover operations are not performed or controlled by this educational simulation.

Technology Used

  • Python 3.12
  • Streamlit
  • JavaScript
  • Three.js and WebGL
  • CesiumJS
  • HTML and CSS
  • Pytest and Playwright

Intended Impact and Creativity

SEVVAAI aims to make planetary exploration more accessible by combining scientific learning, interactive visualization, and mission-based activities. It is designed to work on ordinary student laptops, including systems with integrated graphics, rather than requiring expensive gaming hardware.

Its creative contribution is the integration of planetary data, rover exploration, science activities, and an intelligent mission companion into one educational experience.
